messages:
Maria: Heads-up — after the canary yesterday we're seeing a ~2.5x CPU p95 on collector nodes. correlates with increased span volume from the new fine-grained client instrumentation.
AJ: Ugh. Timeline? which deploy
Maria: deploy-bot: deploy #frontend-traces v3.2.1 at 2024-04-04T03:21Z
deploy-bot: rollout started (canary 5%) -> completed
Kevin: Do we have span counts? per-service? p50/p95 processing time?
Sasha: Quick metrics: host.cpu.user p95 jump from 28% -> 68% on collector pool after 03:30Z. otel.ingest.spans/s ~ 3.8x baseline for frontend-service.
Maria: here's sample from metrics explorer:
```
otel.ingest.spans{service="frontend"}  1200 -> 4600 rps
collector.processing.ms p95  12ms -> 28ms
```
AJ: Did the instrumentation start sending more attributes/tags? larger spans -> more serialization cost
Kevin: Confirmed. frontend added db.query SQL params attr+trace_context in v3.2.1. Span size median went 420b -> 1.3kb
Sasha: Exporter churn also up — exporter queue depth spikes and frequent flushes. suspect batching config not stably grouping larger spans.
Maria: Can we toggle sampling at ingest to protect collectors while we triage?
AJ: We have a runtime flag in collector config: `batch/max_size`, `batch/max_latency`, and `memory/ingest_shedding` — but changing sampling requires coordination with backend tracing accuracy.
Kevin: Proposal: enable a 1% head-based sample for frontend only for 30m to bring CPU back while we fix instrumentation.
Maria: +1 for emergency mitigation. need also to throttle exporter concurrency to avoid CPU scheduling thrash.
Sasha: Agreed. Patch I'll apply:
```
processors:
  probabilistic_sampler:
    sampling_percentage: 1.0
exporters:
  otlp:
    timeout: 30s
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [probabilistic_sampler, batch]
      exporters: [otlp]
```
Maria: Applying to canary now
deploy-bot: user sasha changed config on collector-group/canary at 1712345735
Sasha: canary shows CPU p95 back down to ~32% in 5m window. span ingest rps unchanged but downstream sampling reduces export volume.
Kevin: Good. Next: long term we should add span size histograms and an alert on avg span bytes per service.
AJ: Also want a per-service batching profile: max_batch_bytes + preferred_batch_count heuristics. We currently batch by count only which is bad for variable payload sizes.
Maria: Agreed. Filing follow-up: will add infra ticket and a docs PR for recommended instrumentation size limits and for mantling sensitive attrs.
Kevin: Also consider enabling KV-cache for repeated attribute sets to reduce serialization overhead in exporter pipeline.
Sasha: Note: retention implications — if we sample more, eval dashboards and SLOs need to account for lower observed signal. we should annotate dashboards when sampling active.
Maria: I'll add a temporary annotation on the traces dashboard and create a rollout note in the release channel.
AJ: Great work. Can we revert the frontend change (trim attrs) in next release or push a flag to stop sending SQL params by default?
Kevin: I'll open a PR to add `tracing.exclude_attributes` to the SDK and default to redact `db.statement.params`.
Maria: Thanks team — keeping the canary until PRs land. will close after 24h stable
Sasha: :thumbsup:
Kevin: :+1:
Maria: closing loop later with numbers and ticket links
